title: Is Christian Democracy Finished?
gist: Only a teaser is available: Mueller argues Germany's CDU faces an existential challenge after failing the 5% threshold in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern while the far right finished first in two state elections, and must reconnect with a different part of its history.

insights.claim: The CDU failed to clear the 5% electoral threshold in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, the first such failure in the post-World War II period.
insights.speaker: JAN-WERNER MUELLER
insights.so_what: Signals the erosion of Germany's traditional center-right anchor party.

insights.claim: The CDU collapse happened in a rural state where Angela Merkel chaired the party's state branch for close to seven years.
insights.speaker: JAN-WERNER MUELLER
insights.so_what: Shows Merkel-era strongholds are not insulated from realignment.

insights.claim: The far right finished first in two recent German state elections and may well come to power in one.
insights.speaker: JAN-WERNER MUELLER
insights.so_what: Raises German state-level political risk and spillover to federal coalition dynamics.

insights.claim: The Christian Democratic strategy of caring for all social groups to produce harmony and prevent infighting no longer works because the conditions that enabled it have changed, especially in Germany.
insights.speaker: JAN-WERNER MUELLER
insights.so_what: Catch-all center-right parties face structural, not cyclical, decline.
